findings.title: Envelope accepts noncontributory X25519 recipients
findings.reproduction: Run the bounded Envelope recipient conformance harness against the committed WASM. Encode synthetic u=0 and u=1 as correctly checksummed agreement-public-key URs; call recipient-only protected creation with public entropy and TREZOR.
findings.expected: Reject a recipient that produces an all-zero X25519 shared secret before returning any protected record. Preserve correct recipient and SSKR recovery.
findings.observed: Both rejection assertions fail: protected records are returned. Independent Noble X25519 controls refuse both points. Two ordinary recipient private keys and a two-of-three SSKR quorum recover exact entropy and TREZOR; a wrong key/no permit refuse.
findings.impact: The pinned bc-crypto path feeds the shared secret into HKDF without rejecting zero. For these points, the recipient wrapping key is therefore determined by public constants, so recipient-only confidentiality cannot be relied on; adding another permit does not repair a weak permit. This impact follows from the bound source path and cryptographic semantics. Independent decryption without a private key was not executed. Ordinary generated recipient keys were not shown defective.
findings.recommendedFix: Place one contributory-recipient admission rule in the Rust protection owner, enforce it for every recipient before content-key wrapping, and propagate a clear refusal through all bindings. Prefer checked fallible encapsulation returning an error on the actual all-zero shared secret, including noncanonical equivalent encodings; do not duplicate a page-only blacklist.
findings.requiredVerification: Actual compiled WASM refusal of low-order and equivalent encodings plus ordinary recipient/SSKR controls; library proof that all-zero agreement cannot yield a wrapping key. Canonical source/output verification at release.
findings.qualification: RFC 7748 allows an all-zero check; it does not impose universal syntactic rejection. The finding concerns the application's confidential recipient permit, not noncompliance with a mandatory RFC parsing rule.

findings.title: Core CSV exports label a pending transaction as confirmed
findings.reproduction: Serialize a supported pending Core transaction with null block/time, zero confirmations and both lock flags false through createViewerExport.
findings.expected: Use pending/unconfirmed confirmation status; retain lock information separately.

findings.requiredVerification: Inspect actual single/batch CSV for pending, confirmed and locked combinations with null/zero distinction.

findings.title: Dash Shielded derivation wipes the caller seed and changes output on reuse
findings.reproduction: Call actual deriveDashShielded with one synthetic 64-byte seed and one testnet address. Inspect caller bytes, call again with the same buffer, and compare with a fresh copy of the original seed.
findings.expected: The derivation API borrows caller seed data. Owned copies are wiped without changing future derivation from the same caller input.
findings.observed: The first call zeros the caller buffer. Reuse produces a different address/spending key; a fresh original-seed copy reproduces the first output. Rust mut slice zeroization is copied back by wasm-bindgen glue.
findings.impact: API composition or caller reuse can derive the all-zero-seed wallet after the first call. No UI loss or actual funded output was demonstrated; ordinary callers that supply a disposable copy may avoid the effect.
findings.recommendedFix: Give the WASM boundary an explicit owned copy and wipe it on all paths; keep the caller buffer intact. Retain zeroization of WASM-owned secret memory and document ownership consistently.
findings.requiredVerification: Actual WASM success/failure paths preserve caller bytes; repeated calls and mixed protocol derivations remain deterministic; fresh-copy control and independent pinned Orchard output remain valid.

findings.title: Envelope restoration discards malformed or ambiguous passphrase assertions
findings.reproduction: Pass small correctly typed synthetic Seed Envelope records with a string passphrase, no passphrase, a numeric passphrase object and two distinct string passphrase assertions to the actual committed bundle-recovery WASM.
findings.expected: Absent is distinct from malformed or ambiguous. Restore valid string values; refuse wrong types and duplicate conflicting assertions instead of substituting an empty BIP39 passphrase.
findings.observed: Valid TREZOR and absent controls pass. Both wrong-type and duplicate rejection assertions fail. Rust extract_object_for_predicate(...).ok() converts all extraction errors to None and the JS bundle omits the field.
findings.impact: An accepted record can silently select the entropy-only wallet rather than the intended phrase-plus-passphrase wallet. This affects malformed/imported containers; ordinary well-formed generated controls preserved their passphrase. No external container, real wallet or loss was used.
findings.recommendedFix: Use the library's optional typed extraction contract to distinguish a genuinely absent predicate from extraction failure. Propagate wrong-type/ambiguity errors and preserve valid empty/string semantics through bundle handoff.
findings.requiredVerification: Actual WASM absent/empty/nonempty/wrong-type/duplicate bundle controls and host handoff; encrypted recipient and SSKR recovery preserve exact entropy and passphrase.

findings.title: Incomplete Orchard CSV marks provisional unspent notes as spendable
findings.reproduction: Export a synthetic incomplete FVK ledger snapshot with one recovered incoming note whose provisional spent flag is false.
findings.expected: An incomplete spend scan reports unknown for provisional unspent notes; observed spends remain known.
findings.observed: The summary says partial but the note CSV row says spendable. Complete-FVK, IVK-unknown and observed-spent partial controls pass.
findings.impact: A spend outside the scanned prefix may be overlooked by CSV consumers. No current-chain balance or spending authority was established.
findings.recommendedFix: Require complete FVK coverage before labeling unspent notes spendable; reuse the completeness-aware presentation contract.
findings.requiredVerification: Actual serialized complete/partial FVK, IVK/OVK and known-spent cases remain consistent with summaries and other formats.

findings.title: Missing-code recovery drops the captured BIP39 passphrase during Deriver handoff
findings.reproduction: Use the actual MnemoCodeDecodeTab, MnemoCodeMissingCodes, WalletEvidenceField and MnemoCodeWorkerJob with the bounded synthetic DOM and deferred transport in deriver-probe.test.ts. Input eleven abandon words followed by ?, select the wallet search way with synthetic master fingerprint 01020304 and public BIP39 passphrase TREZOR, and start Search. Assert the captured request contains wallet.evidence={kind:master-fingerprint,value:01020304,network:mainnet} and wallet.passphrase=TREZOR. Resolve the deferred worker with {kind:found,places:Code 12,codes:eleven abandon words followed by about}. Click the actual Use in Generate & Derive button.
findings.expected: A successful recovery selected using a nonempty BIP39 passphrase hands the recovered phrase and that same captured passphrase to Generate & Derive. Missing-code result publication must preserve the wallet factors used by the request.
findings.observed: The coordinator's deriver-probes run passed the exact request guard, then failed the final handoff assertion: the callback was invoked once with only the public phrase, without TREZOR. Source captures wallet.passphrase at recovery-mnemocode-missing-codes.ts:173 but publishes only outcome, format and mode at :206. Decode renders through the phrase-only helper at recovery-mnemocode-decode.ts:328; recovery-workspace-shared.ts:588 invokes useInDeriver(mnemonic). The actual app-bootstrap.ts:40 handoff defaults the omitted passphrase to an empty string and assigns it to the parent field at :48. The live-application field replacement and resulting wrong-wallet selection are source-confirmed consequences of the runtime callback omission.
findings.impact: Automatic handoff selects the phrase with an empty BIP39 passphrase instead of the phrase-plus-TREZOR wallet used for recovery recognition. The recovered phrase remains available and manual passphrase re-entry is a workaround. No wallet loss, fund movement or failure of the cryptographic search was demonstrated.
findings.recommendedFix: Preserve the wallet passphrase captured for the successful missing-code request in its publication contract and pass it through Decode's recovered-phrase handoff. Bind it to the request revision rather than reading a potentially edited passphrase field when Use is clicked. Preserve empty-passphrase and non-wallet search semantics.
findings.requiredVerification: The bounded actual-controller request and handoff probe must pass with nonempty TREZOR and empty-passphrase controls. Verify the actual application handoff populates both parent fields, and that edits or cancellation cannot substitute another request's passphrase. Separately use an authorized public known-wallet control if claiming cryptographic wallet identity; this harness establishes argument preservation, not independent derivation correctness.
findings.releaseBlockingReason: The supported automatic recovery handoff silently replaces a captured nonempty recovery factor with an empty passphrase. Manual re-entry does not satisfy the automatic handoff contract.
findings.skepticRecommendation: The reviewer previously proposed High because the defect breaks automatic recovery to the recognised wallet. The coordinator accepted Medium with releaseBlocking=true because manual re-entry exists and no loss was demonstrated. This candidate records the High proposal only as a skeptic recommendation and retains the coordinator's Medium classification.

The application bootstrap is traced in source; the runtime handoff callback is a spy rather than a complete application instance.

findings.title: MnemoCode Decode retains usable stale results after edits and accepts old-date replies
findings.reproduction: Run the revised Decode group with the actual controllers and synthetic codec/worker. Decode the public phrase of eleven abandon words followed by about in Seedshift mode, English representation and date 01-01-2000. Separately change the input to legal winner thank year wave sausage worth useful legal winner thank yellow, mode to direct, representation to indexes, or date to 02-01-2000; attempt the retained Show phrase, Copy and Use actions. For the late-reply case, start the marked final-word wallet search with captured date 01-01-2000, edit the external dates field to 02-01-2000, resolve the old request with the public phrase and dates=01-01-2000, and attempt the published Use action. Keep the passing control that edits the marked input before resolving its request.
findings.expected: Results and their actions belong to the current Decode inputs. Editing relevant inputs makes old handoff/copy actions unavailable until a fresh Decode, and an old-date worker reply cannot publish a usable result. A retained concealed textarea is permitted if its stale actions are inaccessible; DOM removal is not required by this finding.
findings.observed: In deriver-invalidation-followup, each of the four completed-result edit cases and the pending-date case actually invoked the handoff callback once with the old public phrase, then failed the no-call assertion. The input-edit pending-worker control passed. Source input/mode/format listeners increment Decode's revision but do not invalidate existing result actions. No date listener revises Decode or the missing-code job. The missing-code job watches only its own block, while its request captures the external dates field. The actual markup places that dates field outside the block. The worker job's current-revision guard therefore does not see the date edit, and #showFound publishes the old result.
findings.impact: A corrected code sequence, interpretation or date can coexist with an enabled handoff of a phrase from older inputs. This can send the wrong recovered phrase to Deriver or expose an outdated result through its retained controls. The date-late-reply case demonstrates publication of usable stale output, not merely retention of concealed DOM. No independent wrong-wallet derivation or fund loss was executed.
findings.recommendedFix: Use one input-ownership rule covering codes, effective mode, representation and external dates. On relevant edits invalidate pending publication and deactivate or clear the old result's actions. Preserve deliberate interactions inside recovered results and the existing passing input-edit worker gate.
findings.requiredVerification: All revised completed-edit and pending-date handoff probes must pass, with fresh Decode/current-date positive controls and the existing input-edit cancellation control. Assert stale Use and Copy callbacks cannot execute; do not require DOM removal if equivalent inaccessible output is retained. Verify both found-date and supplied-date outcomes, including changed dates before completion and before Use.

findings.title: Silent Payments publishes results for an outdated parent phrase or passphrase
findings.reproduction: Install the actual main controller and Silent Payments feature with the explicit view contract stub and deferred derivation transport. Set the parent to eleven abandon words followed by about, select Silent Payments, and verify the seed call receives that phrase and an empty passphrase. For completed-output cases, publish sp1-audit-old-source, then change the parent to legal winner thank year wave sausage worth useful legal winner thank yellow with TREZOR, explicitly derive, assert current phrase/passphrase arguments and 64 seed bytes marked 8, and publish sp1-audit-current-source. Separately clear the parent mnemonic or passphrase. For pending-output cases, edit the parent mnemonic to empty or its passphrase to TREZOR before resolving the old request. For Generate, publish the original result, press Generate 12, verify the parent becomes the second phrase, and inspect whether the old Silent Payments result remains available. Do not advance the debounce timers before the invalidation assertions.
findings.expected: Changing the parent phrase or passphrase, including Generate, immediately makes old Silent Payments output unavailable and invalidates old pending publication. A later explicit or automatic derivation reads the current parent fields. Safety does not require an immediate second request or erasure of already hidden text.
findings.observed: All five revised Silent Payments cases failed because the actual feature result remained visible: both completed-parent edit cases, both late-reply cases and Generate. The successful fresh-source controls in the completed-output cases reached their argument, seed-marker and new-address assertions before the failing invalidation assertions. Source supplies dynamic parent-field getters at controller.ts:393 and reads them at silent-payment-feature.ts:104, so fresh derivation uses the current source. Parent edits at controller.ts:984 omit Silent Payments clear/invalidation; its local revision at silent-payment-feature.ts:112 does not detect them. Generate assigns a new phrase without an input event at view.ts:291 and calls ordinary deriveCurrent at controller.ts:1075 without invalidating the existing feature output.
findings.impact: An address or late result derived from the previous parent can remain presented beside a changed wallet source. Complete inputs eventually request an automatic refresh after the controller's debounce; the stale-publication window remains before that refresh. Incomplete inputs prevent the scheduled refresh, and Generate does not refresh this active feature, making the stale state persistent until another explicit action. The harness uses invented address labels and proves source/output association, not incorrect address mathematics or demonstrated fund loss.
findings.recommendedFix: Invalidate Silent Payments' pending revision and make its old result unavailable whenever the parent source changes, including Generate. Reuse the feature's existing clear contract or an equivalent source-revision operation, then schedule or explicitly request derivation from the current source. Preserve source-independent rendering and existing revision protection between feature requests.
findings.requiredVerification: The five revised actual-controller invalidation probes must pass with the fresh-source controls preserved. Cover parent mnemonic and passphrase edits, incomplete input, late replies before debounce, Generate, and later successful derivation from current fields. Hidden old text need not be erased, but it must not remain actionable or become republished by an old request. A claim about BIP352 address correctness needs separate cryptographic evidence owned by the crypto reviewer.

findings.title: Address descriptors reject valid Bech32m Taproot addresses
findings.reproduction: Render the literal BIP86 P2TR script, then compile its checksummed addr(bc1p5cyxnuxmeuwuvkwfem96lqzszd02n6xdcjrs20cac6yqjjwudpxqkedrcr) descriptor through decodeDescriptor.
findings.expected: Recover the exact published script and address, while rejecting corrupted checksums, wrong networks and v1 encoded with Bech32.

findings.impact: A supported Taproot address descriptor cannot be inspected. No incorrectly generated address was demonstrated.
findings.recommendedFix: Use the shared witness-address decoder, then enforce witness version, checksum family and selected network in one owner.

findings.title: Codex32 restoration rejects compatible records in different presentation cases
findings.reproduction: Use official BIP93 shared vector two. Restore both full-uppercase records, both full-lowercase records, then one uppercase and one lowercase record.

findings.observed: Both uniform-case controls restore d1808e096b35b209ca12132b264662a5; the compatible cross-record case pair fails with incompatible prefixes. A within-record mixed-case control correctly refuses.
findings.impact: A valid backup can be rejected after one complete record is transcribed in the other permitted case. Manual whole-record case normalization is a workaround.
findings.recommendedFix: Validate each original record for its case/checksum rules, then normalize admitted semantic prefixes before interpolation. Correct the test that conflates cross-record presentation differences with mixed case within a record.
findings.requiredVerification: Published upper/lower/cross-record combinations plus mixed-within-record, wrong HRP, checksum, identity, threshold and duplicate-index refusals.

findings.title: Unknown Dash PSBT fields acquire unsupported Bitcoin verification semantics
findings.reproduction: Parse a supported Dash v0 one-input/one-output PSBT, adding unknown input keys0x11 and0x13 with empty values. Compare semantic checks and signing analysis to the unmodified control.
findings.expected: Preserve unknown bytes without deriving Bitcoin locktime or signature conclusions from them.

findings.impact: Unvalidated unknown data receives verification/signing labels. This is not signature verification or demonstrated spending capability.
findings.recommendedFix: Use the chain-aware field registry throughout relationship, locktime and signing analysis, not only structural admission.
findings.requiredVerification: Adding each Dash unknown field preserves known semantic conclusions and raw bytes; valid Bitcoin known fields keep their intended behavior.

findings.title: Candidate-list admission buffers an oversized file before rejecting it
findings.reproduction: Use the real importer and panel Select/Open actions with synthetic oversized File metadata and an arrayBuffer spy returning only a small invalid header. No large allocation is needed.
findings.expected: Read only a bounded header and reject unsupported file sizes before whole-file buffering.
findings.observed: All three entry points call arrayBuffer once before rejection. The subsequent 64 KiB header restriction cannot bound this initial allocation.
findings.impact: A locally selected untrusted large file can consume excessive memory before format rejection. Host exhaustion was not attempted; no remote trigger or secret egress was shown. The importer accepts an arrayBuffer-only interface, so the primary admission fix belongs to the actual file selection/Open owner and its format limits.
findings.recommendedFix: Read a bounded header slice, derive one format-owned encrypted/plaintext size ceiling, and enforce it before and during buffering/decryption.
findings.requiredVerification: Oversized metadata refuses without arrayBuffer; valid small files and boundary-size headers still import; streaming/body size is bounded.

findings.title: Codex32 zero-padded random basis reveals a secret bit below threshold
findings.reproduction: Enumerate the two final-byte low-bit choices of the random basis for a synthetic 32-byte two-of-two share set, twice for secrets differing only in their final bit. Inspect the final payload symbol of index c and retain exact two-share restoration controls.
findings.expected: The distribution of a below-threshold share must not identify a bit of the secret. Random basis elements must cover the full GF(32) payload symbol space, including padding positions.
findings.observed: The last-symbol supports are disjoint: secret bit0 gives p/q and bit1 gives 3/s. All four two-share round-trip controls restore exact inputs. from_seed supplies zero padding for the last four bits of both the master and the random basis.
findings.impact: For this supported 256-bit two-of-two layout, one index-c share identifies the secret's last bit. This is a one-bit threshold secrecy violation, not recovery of an entire mnemonic or demonstrated fund loss. The fixture enumerates the last-symbol projection; pointwise GF(32) interpolation makes other payload symbols irrelevant to that projection. No large statistical run was used.
findings.recommendedFix: Generate random basis records with independent uniform GF(32) symbols including padding positions, using one validated reference-implementation entry point. Keep canonical master data encoding, valid BIP93 checksums and interoperability.
findings.requiredVerification: Independent finite-field projection check and below-threshold secrecy cases at every non-byte-aligned supported length, including other thresholds/indexes; known BIP93 values and reconstruction/refusal tests.

findings.title: Early Orchard preparation errors bypass owned-secret cleanup
findings.reproduction: Capture the decoder-owned synthetic viewing-key buffer and fail each note field width; separately have shielded derivation throw after capturing its wrapper-owned seed copy.
findings.expected: Owned secret allocations enter a wiping scope immediately; caller-owned inputs remain unchanged.

In-scope engine/guard failures wipe correctly, and the supplied caller seed stays unchanged. The viewing buffer retained95nonzero bytes out of96; the seed copy retained64outof64.

Provider admission limits ordinary malformed-note reachability in Discovery; arbitrary library inputs and injected failures establish ownership gaps. The harness retained references to observe missing explicit wiping; it cannot establish post-GC persistence or real trap frequency.

findings.title: Independent recovery secret controls remain revealed after blur or tab hiding
findings.reproduction: Run the six concealment cases in the original deriver-probes harness. Install the actual main controller with its two global reveal flags initially false. Separately install an actual manual recovery installSecretToggle containing the public abandon/about phrase, render an actual recovered phrase with renderRecoveredMnemonic, or construct an actual MHFE PasswordField containing TREZOR. Click each local Show control and verify it reveals its value. Dispatch window blur, or set document.visibilityState=hidden and dispatch visibilitychange. Inspect the conceal class, password input type and local reveal state.
findings.expected: Locally revealed recovery phrases, recovered results and password fields return to their concealed state on window blur or tab hiding, with secret copy actions disabled again. Their independent reveal controls must not depend on the main Deriver's reveal flags being true.
findings.observed: The coordinator's original run reached all six intended concealment assertions after successful local-reveal setup: manual and recovered phrases still lacked the concealed class, and PasswordField still had type=text, on both blur and hidden. The actual controller lifecycle listeners were installed in those probes. Source initializes its global flags false at controller.ts:152 and performs no conceal operation while they remain false at :1119. Its view conceal methods affect only the main source and ordinary result root. The actual workspace installs LinkedSources handlers, but they conceal only linked-source cards in that class's private revealed map. MHFE wallet-list conceal handlers target only their own result container. Neither covers these manual controls, Decode results or PasswordField instances.
findings.impact: Secret text can remain visually exposed when the person leaves the window or hides the tab, contrary to the documented visual-protection contract. This is a limited visual confidentiality defect; no network disclosure, persistence compromise, browser screenshot disclosure or loss was demonstrated. Linked-source cards and MHFE wallet-list results with their own conceal handlers are not included in this allegation.
findings.recommendedFix: Give independent recovery reveal controls a shared lifecycle conceal registration that resets their local reveal state, concealment, diagnostics and secret copy availability. Install it through the real workspace and cover dynamically rendered recovered results. Preserve the deliberately separate scopes and existing linked-source/wallet-list handlers.
findings.requiredVerification: Retain the six bounded component/controller cases and add an actual workspace integration acceptance check for a manual source, a Decode result and an MHFE password field with global reveal flags false. Confirm blur and visibility hiding reconceal these controls and disable Copy. Keep linked-source and wallet-list positive controls. Real rendering, browser event delivery and clipboard permissions require separately authorized browser verification.

findings.title: Recovery tab installer omits keyboard navigation while removing inactive tabs from Tab order
findings.reproduction: Use the actual recovery installTabs with three synthetic role=tab buttons and three role=tabpanel sections. Click and focus the starting tab, assert one selected tab and one tabindex=0, then dispatch ArrowRight from index 0, ArrowLeft from index 0, Home from index 2 or End from index 0. Expect selected tab indexes 1, 2, 0 and 2 respectively, corresponding focus and matching panel visibility.
findings.expected: The actual recovery tabs implement the shared WAI-ARIA tab contract: arrow keys move selection/focus with wrapping, Home/End reach the first/last tab, and the selected panel follows. Removing inactive tabs from the normal Tab order requires another keyboard route to them.
findings.observed: All four coordinator-run keyboard cases failed at the intended next-tab aria-selected assertion after click selection and roving tabindex setup passed. Source installTabs installs only click listeners. markTab sets inactive tabs to tabindex=-1, while isTabKey/tabIndexAfter define the required arrow/Home/End behavior. Actual recovery workspace uses this installer for both its main recovery tabs and each backup method's operation tabs. The controller's separate keyboard handler is attached to ordinary protocolTabs, not the recovery tab lists.
findings.impact: Keyboard users following normal Tab navigation cannot reach inactive recovery/operation tabs, and their expected arrow/Home/End alternatives do nothing. Mouse navigation still works. No browser accessibility-tree or assistive-technology assessment was executed.
findings.recommendedFix: Wire the recovery installer to the existing shared tab-key helpers, updating selected tab, panel and focus together and preventing the handled key's default behavior. Preserve its current click path and single tabindex=0 invariant rather than duplicating navigation rules.
findings.requiredVerification: All four actual-installer keyboard cases must pass with click, focus and panel assertions. Add actual workspace coverage for both recovery and operation tab lists and disabled/empty cases where applicable. Verify browser keyboard focus and accessibility behavior separately when browser execution is authorized.

The DOM support models events, ARIA attributes, tabIndex and focus but not native key defaults, browser accessibility trees or assistive-technology interaction.

remediation.explanation: The original verification applied to a local MHFE0.5.1 integration. The current MHFE0.6.0 signed release pin leaves ARCHITECTURE's unreleased-local/CI-refuses sentence stale again. Preserve the historical verified record; this is a current recurrence requiring a documentation correction under the existing ID, not a new historical test execution.

limitations: Full audit scope was reviewed with targeted/security-level execution. This is an incomplete baseline audit, not release acceptance or independent certification.

No real browsers, viewports, screenshots, accessibility trees, startup controls or actual browser worker/CSP lifecycle were executed at the owner's request. Controller probes use bounded fake DOM/worker replies; source integration was challenged separately.
